blockers.what: The per-job guard checks that a gate is mentioned in a job's run lines, not that it runs and can fail the job. One-line edits that disarm the Windows job or one of its gates leave tools/ci.test.ts green: job-level `if: false`; job-level `continue-on-error: true`; step-level `continue-on-error: true`; step-level `if: false`; `run: pnpm lint || exit 0`; `run: pnpm typecheck; exit 0`; `run: pnpm package:check || true`; `run: echo pnpm brand:lint`; `run: node tools/build.mjs --help`; `run: echo docs/ux/lint.py`. The test titled 'would notice a Windows job cut down, moved or removed' (tools/ci.test.ts:210) claims more than gatesMissingFrom delivers; `echo pnpm brand:lint` is the same 'mention rather than use' defect the shares() docstring at :45-53 names (tools/ci.test.ts:190-196 (gatesMissingFrom: substring includes over commandsIn) and :198-219 (no check on job or step `if:` / `continue-on-error:`), found by the `unit` tier)

The self-test at tools/ci.test.ts:210-219 builds its plants with exact-string replace on `run: pnpm test\n` and `run: pnpm i18n:sweep\n`. Any legitimate edit to either line (a flag, a comment after it) makes replace a no-op and fails the self-test with a misleading message; it is also why `pnpm test || exit 0` and `pnpm test tools/ci.test.ts` appear caught: they are caught by the self-test losing its anchor, not by the guard (verified: the only failing test for that plant is 'would notice a Windows job cut down, moved or removed') (tools/ci.test.ts:210-219, found by the `unit` tier)

The Windows `pnpm test` step passes with 30 skipped tests against 4 on Linux in the same run (3046 passed | 30 skipped of 3076 on Windows; 3074 passed | 4 skipped of 3078 on Linux), and 2 tests are not registered at all on Windows.
